title: Relative equivalence-prism extension with all vertices prescribed
statement:
Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, equivalence edges and degreewise products of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and pushouts (colimits of spans) of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $p:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a map between quasicategories which lifts every inner horn $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, $0<i<n$. Let $A\subseteq B$ be a simplicial subset of a small simplicial set, containing every vertex of $B$, and let $\epsilon\in\{0,1\}$. Set
$$P_\epsilon=(\Delta^1\times A)\amalg_{\{\epsilon\}\times A}(\{\epsilon\}\times B).$$
Suppose $h_0:P_\epsilon\to\mathcal C$ and $g:\Delta^1\times B\to\mathcal D$ satisfy $ph_0=g|_{P_\epsilon}$. If for every vertex $b\in B$ the edge $h_0|_{\Delta^1\times\{b\}}$ is an equivalence in $\mathcal C$, then there exists $h:\Delta^1\times B\to\mathcal C$ with $h|_{P_\epsilon}=h_0$ and $ph=g$ exactly.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.5.8 (Kerodon Tag 01NX), with its vertexwise hypothesis strengthened to all vertices; epsilon=1 is the displayed statement and epsilon=0 is its opposite-simplicial-set dual. Read the full statement and proof online on 2026-10-17. Kerodon tags, not Stacks tags; no Stacks statement of this quasicategorical lemma was found. WANTED: archived source.

proof.text: First take $\epsilon=1$. The two inclusions defining $P_1$ are inclusions of simplicial subsets of $\Delta^1\times B$, and their intersection is $\{1\}\times A$. Its pushout is their union: in each degree a pair of maps agreeing on the intersection defines a unique map on the union, and these maps commute with operators on each piece. This verifies the colimit property of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and identifies the given $h_0$ with data on that union. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells] to $A\hookrightarrow B$, obtaining $Z_0=A$, $Z_n\hookrightarrow Z_{n+1}$ and colimit $B$. There are no zero-dimensional cells because every vertex belongs to $A$, so $Z_1=A$. We construct compatible $H_n:\Delta^1\times Z_n\to\mathcal C$ over $g$, agreeing with $h_0$ on $\Delta^1\times A$ and on $\{1\}\times Z_n$. Set $H_0=H_1=h_0|_{\Delta^1\times A}$. The subsequent steps perform the induction for each cell dimension $n\geq1$. The small simplicial set $B$ supplies a small set of choices of fillers.

source.place: Proof, extension ordered by subcomplexes; expanded here by the existing relative skeletal filtration instead of Zorn.

proof.text: Fix a cell in the pushout at the stage $Z_n\hookrightarrow Z_{n+1}$, where $n\geq1$, and let $\tau:\Delta^n\to Z_{n+1}\hookrightarrow B$ be its characteristic map from that pushout. The attaching map sends its boundary into $Z_n$ by [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells]. No additional property of the cell indexing, or injectivity of $\tau$, is needed. Pull back $H_n$ along that boundary and $h_0|_{\{1\}\times B}$ along $\tau$. These maps agree on $\{1\}\times\partial\Delta^n$, and give a map $v$ on $X_0=(\Delta^1\times\partial\Delta^n)\cup(\{1\}\times\Delta^n)$, over $g_\tau=g(1\times\tau)$. Use [lem-coef-infinity-right-prism-boundary] with $m=n$. It supplies the successive pushouts along $\Lambda_{q+1}^{n+1}\hookrightarrow\Delta^{n+1}$ and the specified simplices $\sigma_q$, for $0\leq q\leq n$. Starting from $v_0=v$, when $q<n$ the horn index satisfies $0<q+1<n+1$. The hypothesis on $p$ therefore supplies a filler of the horn map $v_q\sigma_q|_{\Lambda_{q+1}^{n+1}}$ over the actual simplex $g_\tau\sigma_q$. Glue that filler with $v_q$ by the cited pushout universal property to obtain $v_{q+1}$. Both composites to $\mathcal D$ agree with $g_\tau$ on the old subset and the attached simplex, hence everywhere by uniqueness in the same pushout.

source.place: Proof, reduction to a boundary inclusion and the inner-horn stages of the standard prism filtration.

proof.text: At $q=n$, the last attachment is $\Lambda_{n+1}^{n+1}\hookrightarrow\Delta^{n+1}$. Its dimension is $n+1\geq2$. The formula for $\sigma_n$ in [lem-coef-infinity-right-prism-boundary] sends its last two vertices to $(0,n)$ and $(1,n)$, so it sends the final ordered edge exactly to $\Delta^1\times\{n\}$. Indeed maps $[1]\to[1]$ and $[1]\to[n]$ are determined by their endpoints, using [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The vertex $\tau(n)$ belongs to $A$ because every vertex of $B$ does, and the item hypothesis says its prescribed vertical edge is an equivalence; for $n\geq1$ this vertex also belongs to the boundary. Thus this entire vertical edge is already in $X_0$, and its image under $v_n$ is the original equivalence $h_0|_{\Delta^1\times\{\tau(n)\}}$. Apply [lem-cbc-inner-fibration-equivalence-outer-horn-lift], whose final-horn clause has dimension $n+1$, to the horn map $v_n\sigma_n$ and base simplex $g_\tau\sigma_n$. It gives a filler over that precise base simplex. The last pushout gives $V_\tau:\Delta^1\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal C$ extending $v$ and satisfying $pV_\tau=g_\tau$. This completes the cell calculation; no lifting of new vertex edges is requested.

source.place: Proof, final outer-horn stage, using the relative theorem 01H0 with its final-edge hypothesis checked explicitly.

proof.text: Choose such a $V_\tau$ for every cell at this stage and glue it with $H_n$. Here is the degreewise construction from the pushout in [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells], including cells whose maps into $B$ identify vertices or faces. The simplicial set obtained degreewise from $(Z_n)_k\amalg\coprod_\tau(\Delta^n)_k$ by the boundary identifications has the required pushout property: compatible maps define a unique function on classes in every degree, and these functions are simplicial on each summand. By [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] it is therefore canonically $Z_{n+1}$. In degree $k$ define the value at $(t,z)$ using $H_n(t,z)$ on the old summand, and $V_\tau(t,u)$ on the simplex summand. These values agree under every boundary identification because $V_\tau$ extends the pulled-back boundary map. They therefore give a unique function on $(\Delta^1)_k\times(Z_{n+1})_k$; operators commute with it on every representative. This defines $H_{n+1}$. On each representative $pH_{n+1}=g$, its terminal-endpoint restriction is $h_0$, and it extends $H_n$. The prescribed vertical edges at final vertices of newly attached simplices remain unchanged; each such edge is the original equivalence supplied by the hypothesis.

source.place: Proof, passage from one boundary-prism filler to arbitrary attachments; quotient construction spells out preservation of this pushout by the degreewise product.

proof.text: The increasing union $Z_\infty=\bigcup_n Z_n$ is $B$. To justify this directly from [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells], the degreewise union is a simplicial subset of $B$ and is a colimit of the sequence: compatible maps define the unique map on its elements by their values at any containing stage, independently of the stage. Its colimit property and the stated colimit $B$ identify its inclusion with an isomorphism by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For $z\in B_k$ choose a stage containing it and set $h_k(t,z)=(H_n)_k(t,z)$. Compatibility makes the value independent of the choice; each operator preserves the chosen stage and commutes with its $H_n$, so $h$ is simplicial. The identities $ph=g$ and $h|_{P_1}=h_0$ hold at every stage and hence exactly on the union. This proves the assertion for $\epsilon=1$, including infinitely many cells and unbounded dimension.

source.place: Proof, maximality/exhaustion step; rewritten as the compatible union of relative skeleta.

proof.text: For $\epsilon=0$ use the opposite involution explicitly. For $\alpha:[r]\to[s]$ set $\alpha^{\mathrm{rev}}(j)=s-\alpha(r-j)$; it is monotone, respects identities and compositions, and applying it twice gives $\alpha$. Define $(X^{\mathrm{op}})_r=X_r$ with operator $X(\alpha^{\mathrm{rev}})$. This commutes degreewise with products, unions and the defining pushout. The bijection on standard simplices given by $f\mapsto f^{\mathrm{rev}}$ identifies $(\Delta^s)^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $\Delta^s$ and carries $(\Lambda_i^s)^{\mathrm{op}}$ to $\Lambda_{s-i}^s$, by the omitted-vertex definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Hence $p^{\mathrm{op}}$ still lifts inner horns and its source and target are quasicategories. Reversing each inverse edge and the two witness triangles preserves the equivalence-edge condition. Under the interval identification, endpoint $0$ becomes endpoint $1$, and $(P_0)^{\mathrm{op}}$ identifies with $P_1$ for $A^{\mathrm{op}}\subseteq B^{\mathrm{op}}$; every prescribed vertical equivalence remains an equivalence for $A^{\mathrm{op}}\subseteq B^{\mathrm{op}}$. Apply the proved $\epsilon=1$ case to $(p^{\mathrm{op}},h_0^{\mathrm{op}},g^{\mathrm{op}})$. Applying the involution again to its filler yields the required $\epsilon=0$ filler, with both restriction and base-map equations unchanged as exact equalities. If $A=B$ the given map is already the filler; empty $B$ is included.

source.place: Opposite-simplicial-set dual, with operator formula and horn, endpoint and equivalence checks written out.

Steps 1-5 realize the relative simplex-attachment calculation of Kerodon 01NX needed by the parent isofibration exponentiation; Step 6 supplies its source-fixed dual. This is supporting coherent-diagram infrastructure for the inherited paragraph, not a replacement of a geometric unit step.
